propositions: a committed uv.lock pins transitive dependencies, causing any published advisory against a pinned version to block all in-flight changes regardless of whether they touch the dependency map
the retry logic in pip-audit only retries DB-unreachable failures, so real findings cannot be rechecked, making recheck the first instinct of every author and the single most time-wasting property

constraint-dependencies can only narrow an existing constraint set and returns UNSATISFIABLE as expected output, which reads as proof the upgrade is impossible but proves nothing; override-dependencies is the correct instrument to replace an offending requirement

the Gerrit verify lane must block on an advisory only when a change touches the dependency map (uv.lock, pyproject.toml, requirements/constraints files), not on every in-flight change, while the scheduled main lane must block releases on outstanding advisories

a real advisory in the shipped environment is a correct gate finding; the problem is response latency caused by punishing the wrong people, so the solution is lane-specific blocking posture rather than disabling the gate

override-dependencies must carry a REMOVE-WHEN condition and a justification naming the advisory and capping package, and a mechanism must exist to notice when the condition is met rather than relying on someone happening to re-test
